Ava (support): Sorry to ping, AcmeSync reported a sudden surge of 429s during their nightly bulk sync at ~00:30 UTC. They say it started when their worker pool kicked off a fanout job.
Jordan (sre): Can you paste the sample responses or headers? 429s could be RPM windowing or a sudden token consumption spike.
Ava (support): Copied from customer logs: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nDate: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 00:31:02 GMT\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 600\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 60`
Ava (support): They also included this curl repro (trimmed):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx" -d '{"input": "ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Samir (cust): We trigger ~800 requests in a 30s window across 40 worker processes. We thought burst would be allowed for a few seconds.
Maya (eng): If X-RateLimit-Remaining is 0 and Reset is small, this looks like RPM enforcement. Are they on a shared hosted plan or dedicated?
Ava (support): Customer on hosted free/standard tier (metered) — not Dedicated.
Jordan (sre): Ok. Two likely vectors: 1) request burst causing RPM window to be exhausted in that minute; 2) tokens/spike from long-context requests counted against TPM. Do they send many short requests or few large ones?
Samir (cust): Mostly small requests (few hundred tokens each) but we do concurrent fanout.
Maya (eng): Concurrency + minute-aligned cron-like fanout = classic minute-bucket exhaustion. Recommend the customer stagger workers slightly or add jitter.
Ava (support): Suggested immediate mitigations to customer: reduce concurrency to <10 workers, add randomized jitter 0-5s, and exponential backoff on 429s with full-jitter.
Samir (cust): Can you also confirm if we should increase per-minute quota? We can't redesign tonight.
Jordan (sre): We can offer a temporary quota bump for a few hours while they roll a config change. Need their org id and target window.
Ava (support): Asking for org id now.
ops-bot: AUTO: quota-bump-request created #INC-2026-1123 by Ava
Ava (support): Also asked for request IDs from when they hit 429 to correlate in logs.
Samir (cust): Provided request ids: r_20260317_003100_01, r_20260317_003101_22, r_20260317_003102_09
Jordan (sre): Pulling logs for those request ids. `kubectl logs -l app=edge-proxy -n prod --since=10m | rg r_20260317_0031`
Jordan (sre): Observing a huge spike of concurrent inbound TCP connections from the customer's IP range at 00:30: frequent short-lived connections. Edge proxy shows 429s originating at the rate limiter.
Maya (eng): Two long-term options: 1) recommend Dedicated / reserved capacity if they need predictable high TPS; 2) if they must stay on hosted, we can advise using a client-side queue + token bucket to shape requests into steady rate.
Ava (support): Customer asked about any platform-level smoothing we can do to reduce sudden minute-boundary penalties.
Jordan (sre): We have global smoothing on some routes but not across all hosted tenants—makes isolation tricky. For now, we can do a one-off soft cap increase for the upcoming window and monitor. This buys them time to roll jitter.
Maya (eng): Also flagging that if requests use streaming, maintaining long-lived streams reduces per-request overhead and helps avoid RPM spikes.
Samir (cust): We're using short-lived HTTP calls per job. Might be able to switch to multiplexed connections. Good to know.
Ava (support): Action items: 1) temporary quota increase for tonight (ops-bot created INC). 2) Provide customer best-practices doc snippet for smoothing. 3) SRE/Eng to correlate logs and confirm no bug on our rate windowing.
Jordan (sre): I'll leave a short diagnostic note: `confirmed rate limiter tripped on minute bucket; no evidence of double-charging tokens; edge proxy accepted X concurrent streams ~420 at peak`
Maya (eng): I'll open ENG ticket to evaluate whether we can add short burst credits for first 10s of heavy fanout patterns (feature request).
ops-bot: AUTO: ENG-4571 created by Maya — "burst-credits-for-hosted-tenants"
Samir (cust): Thanks. If you can bump us for tonight that would be great. We'll also start rolling jitter tomorrow morning.
Ava (support): Bump applied: +50% RPM for 2 hours (until 02:30 UTC). Monitor and revert if not needed. :thumbsup:
Samir (cust): Seeing 200->0 429s in our dashboard after the bump. We'll rely on this window to deploy stagger. Thank you!
Jordan (sre): Follow-up: schedule a quick 15m post-mortem with customer tomorrow to review traffic pattern and suggest architectural fixes.
Ava (support): Noted. Closing on support side after the post-mortem.
Maya (eng): FYI — engineering will pick up ENG-4571 in the next sprint for feasibility.
Samir (cust): Appreciate the quick help.
Ava (support): Closing notes: recommended client-side rules (send rate <= 600 RPM, max concurrency 12, jitter 0-6s, exponential backoff with full jitter starting at 500ms). I'll paste this as a short guide in the ticket.
